Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the recap - that matches our notes. A few follow-ups from security/ops before we schedule the deep-dive: 

1) PII handling: can you confirm whether any customer-provided content (including user prompts) is ever replicated to non-pinned regions for indexing/analytics? We need a strong guarantee that EU customer prompts are not replicated to US compute/storage outside of the EU tenant boundary.

2) Data retention: what's the minimum configurable retention window for logs and request payloads? We need to support a 90-day retention for debug logs and a 13-month retention for audit logs; ability to reduce is fine, but not increase beyond customer-defined windows.

3) Logging & access controls: how granular are access logs? Do they show user-level identity for who accessed logs/requests, and are logs exportable to our SIEM (S3-compatible endpoint or SFTP)?

4) Cross-region failover: for DR, can you outline how KV caches are handled during a failover and whether there is any possibility of data being served from a secondary region that would violate residency for a short window?

If possible, please send short answers to the above and then we'll pick 2-3 people from security/infra to join the deep-dive.

Best,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Cloud Security | Acme Bank

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: region pinning & next steps

Hi Olivia - thanks for the great questions. High-level answers below; Marissa and Aditya will add technical depth in the deep-dive.

1) PII replication: Redwood's region pinning operates at the tenant/project level. By default, customer data (including prompts and inferred embeddings/indices) is kept within the pinned region. We do not replicate production request payloads to non-pinned regions for indexing. Replication is only performed to a configured backup region (you explicitly enable backups) and those replicas are also subject to the same access controls and encryption rules.

2) Retention windows: debug/request payload logs are configurable per-tenant. Minimum configurable retention we support now is 7 days; we can configure 90 days for debug logs and 13 months for audit logs as part of an enterprise plan and retention policy SLA. We can also integrate with your log archival to your S3 bucket for longer-term retention.

3) Logging & access controls: Access logs include user identity, action, timestamp, and originating IP. Logs are exportable via S3-compatible push (or we can provide an SFTP endpoint). We can add structured fields your SIEM requires in the log payload.

4) Cross-region failover and KV caches: In planned failover (read-only maintenance), KV caches are regenerated in the target region from persisted checkpoints. In unplanned failover, there's a small window where in-flight KV state may be lost and the system will rebuild from last persistent snapshot; we can minimize that window by increasing checkpoint frequency. For strict residency, we offer a configuration where failover is limited to regions within the same legal boundary (e.g., EU only) - this prevents serving from a non-EU region for EU tenants.

Attached the region pinning design doc and a short MR scoping sheet (acme_mrp_scoping_sheet.xlsx) - fills in defaults we discussed. If this looks good, can Marissa schedule a 60-min deep-dive next week with your security and infra leads?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: region pinning & next steps -- technical notes

Hi Olivia,

Adding a few technical clarifications from the SE side so your team can evaluate tradeoffs before the deep-dive:

- Backup behavior: snapshots are incremental and encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys when requested. Backups can be restricted to the same legal region. We retain a configurable number of snapshots; we typically recommend daily snapshots with a 30-day rolling window for fast recovery plus weekly/monthly archival to your S3.

- Failover RTO/RPO: Typical RTO for automatic failover (within same legal boundary) is 5-15 minutes depending on checkpoint cadence and model warmup. RPO depends on snapshot cadence - with 1-min checkpoints we can approach near-zero RPO for in-memory state that we persist frequently, but this has cost/IO tradeoffs.

- Cache & session state: short-lived KV cache entries (session tokens, partial decoding state) are not replicated continuously; they are reconstructed post-failover. For workflows that cannot tolerate reconstruction, we recommend an active-active model within the same boundary (costly) or using an explicit replication window with controlled data residency.

- QA suggestion: please bring a sample of your session/usage profile (typical sequence lengths, tokens/sec, proportion of PII-containing prompts) into the deep-dive so we can calibrate checkpoint cadence and cache sizing.

Happy to lead the deep-dive and walk through the architecture diagram. Proposed slots: Tue 2026-11-24 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 2026-11-25 09:00-10:00 PT. Which works for you?
